hypotheses.justification: The statement stays true for every real q once 0 < η is kept. Put x = η*q. Complex cpow is the principal root, so for x ≥ 0 we get x^(1/2) = √x. For x < 0 it is i·√(-x), and (3x/4)^(1/2) = i·√(-3x/4). The product of the two roots is then -√(-x)·√(-3x/4) = -(√3/2)|x| = (√3/2)x, which is the same value as in the x ≥ 0 case. So the denominator is (√3/2)·η·q in all cases. For q ≠ 0 the left side is η/((√3/2)ηq) = 2/(√3 q), using η ≠ 0, which equals the right side. For q = 0 both sides are 0: the complex 0^(1/2) is 0, 1/0 = 0 in ℂ, and 2/(√3·0) = 0 in ℝ. A proof without hq would split on the sign of η*q. For x < 0 it would use Complex.ofReal_cpow_of_nonpos (or the square-root identity) in place of Complex.ofReal_cpow, and the final algebra would be done directly rather than by calling eta_times_prefactor, which needs hq. The hypothesis hη cannot be dropped: for η = 0 and q > 0 the left side is 0 and the right side is nonzero.
